# basketball-shootout-program-standard

| | |
|---|---|
| Benchmark | Embodied Agent Olympiad |
| Mode | standard (`eai-standard-turn/1.0`) |
| Twin | — (standard only: Olympiad sports have no privileged twin) |
| Simulator / robot | `MuJoCo 3.3.7 (ball with quadratic drag and Magnus force; rim, backboard, floor and defender contacts)` / `none` |
| Family / instance | `basketball_single` |

## Task
A declared shooting machine (a launcher like Toyota's CUE robots) on a 1 m pedestal shoots from five spots, mid-range to beyond the three-point line, past a static defender, finding the hoop in the camera images; every make counts 1; format `single` (seats A),
action level `low`, program play. Generated by `tools/generate.py` from
`sports/basketball/sport.toml`; do not edit by hand.

Deviations from the rulebook:

|---|---|---|

## Difficulty
Set at run time: the seed (`RO_SEED`; it draws the match's random conditions).

## Reference solution
`solution/solve.sh` runs the sport's reference player (`solution/builtin_players.py`) through the core's client
(`solution/ro_client.py`): camera images and `/spec` only.

## Verification
The `sim` service (the v0.2 core, `environment/sim/core/`) records the match (`episode.jsonl`) and a fresh process
replays it (state hash); the verifier (`tests/grade.py` = `core/grading.py`, no network) writes the common reward
fields (`success`, `valid_trial`, `deterministic`, `<seat>_won`, ...) and the sport's fields (`tests/sport_grade.py`).

## Details
| | |
|---|---|
| Rules | [FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2024 (Art. 16, goal); closest standard contest: FIBA 3x3 Shoot-out Contest](https://assets.fiba.basketball/image/upload/documents-corporate-fiba-official-rules-2024-v10a.pdf) version 2024 v1.0a |
| id | rule | deviation |
| D1 | FIBA 3x3 Shoot-out Contest | a shooting contest instead of a game: 10 shots, two from each of five spots |
| D2 | Art. 16.2.1 | every make counts 1, from any spot, instead of 2 or 3 points by the release area |
| D3 | Art. 2 | NBA court markings and equipment sizes (FIBA: a 6.75 m three-point arc and a 1.80 m backboard) |
| D4 | Art. 33 (contact) | a static defender with its hands up stands on the line from the shooter to the hoop; a ball that touches it first is blocked and does not count (instead of live defence) |
| D5 | Art. 29 (shot clock) | time is a chess clock (60 minutes, running while the shootout is on) instead of a shot clock |
| D7 | Art. 4 (teams: the players) | the shooter is a declared shooting machine, like Toyota's CUE basketball robots, not a player: you set its release (yaw, elevation, speed up to 14 m/s, spin) and it releases the ball from its muzzle with a stated execution scatter; 14 m/s is within what a real shooting robot reaches (CUE6's 24.55 m record shot needs about 20 m/s with this sport's drag), while a robot arm's hand (a Franka Panda: about 2 m/s) could not reach the hoop from any spot |
